hushfacebook.title: v0.19.0
hushfacebook.body:
This one needs Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer, so update Manager before you patch. Posts can get Save and Download buttons under them, and new switches take Like, Comment, Share or Send off posts and reels, hide posts from Pages or drop the dislike on comments. Feed videos can get a cast button, downloads can go to an SD card, and 32-bit phones work now. You can also pick your own badge and logo colors, sort reels by most liked and copy a reel's whole caption.

New in this release

- New `Badge and logo colors` lets you pick your own color for the red count badges on the tabs and for the blue Facebook logo at the top of Home. Type a color code like #2ECC71 in `Badge color` or `Logo color` under Appearance and restart Facebook. Left blank, both keep Facebook's colors, and settings backups carry them (Refs #263).

- Facebook 584.0.0.51.56 now works on 32-bit phones too. The armeabi-v7a Android 11+ bundle, build 475817404, is declared next to the arm64 build 475817393, and every patch applies to it. Contributed by toidicakhia (Refs #254).

- `Hide the Create button` under Tabs and navigation takes the + button for new posts, reels and stories out of the top bar, on both versions of the bar Facebook hands out. It starts off and shows after a restart (Refs #257).

- A reel's More menu has `Copy caption` now. It copies the whole caption, including the part hidden behind See more, so there's no more screenshotting a long caption to get its text. It's on by default, and `Copy reel captions` under Reels and Watch turns it off (Refs #240).

- You can pick a plain home screen icon when you patch. The `Icon style` option of Hushfacebook settings in Morphe draws Facebook's "f" white on black or black on white, and `Facebook colors` (the default) leaves the icon alone. Themed icons on Android 13 and up still work with either one (Refs #278).

- New `Show full post text` puts a long post's whole text in the feed, so there's no See more to tap. It starts off. Turn it on under News feed in Hushfacebook's settings, and the diagnostic report counts each post it kept whole (Refs #268).

- Downloads can go to an SD card. Pick it in `Save on`, right above `Save to` under Downloads, and videos and photos land on the card in the same folders they'd use on the phone. The phone's storage stays the default. If the card is out of the phone, saves go to the phone's storage until you put it back, so a save never fails over a missing card (Refs #274).

- Reels can pause while you read their comments. Turn on `Pause reels while comments are open` under Comments and writing, and a playing reel stops when its comments open and picks up from the same spot when you close them. A reel you start yourself under the comments keeps playing (Refs #266).

- `Words to hide` and `Words that keep a post` have a test box under the list now. Paste a post's text and it says whether that post would hide or stay, and which list decided, using the list as you've typed it so far, before you tap Save. Nothing you paste gets saved, and only its first 16,384 characters are checked.

- `Newest reels first` is called `Sort loaded reels` now, and a `Reels order` row right under it picks how: `Newest` (the old behavior and still the default) or `Most liked`. It still only reorders the reels Facebook has already loaded for you. A reel without the count it's sorted by keeps Facebook's spot for it. Search finds the switch by its old name too, and settings backups carry the order (Refs #134).

- Feed videos can get a cast button. Facebook took its own casting out, so `Cast button on feed videos` under Video and audio puts a button in the video's top right corner that hands it to a casting app you already have, like Web Video Caster, and that app sends it to your TV. It starts off and needs a build with the video download patch. If the video hasn't loaded a file yet, it says so and asks you to play it for a moment first (Refs #182).

- Posts can have Save and Download buttons under them now, next to Like, Comment and Share. `Save button under posts` adds Facebook's own Save button, filled bookmark and all. `Download button under posts` adds a Download button to posts with a video or photos, and it saves them the same way the post's menu does (an album saves every photo). Both are under News feed and start off. Download needs a build with the video or photo download patch, and posts with nothing to save don't get the button. Right below them, `Hide Like under posts`, `Hide Comment under posts`, `Hide Share under posts` and `Hide Send under posts` each take one button out of that row in the feed. Reels get the same under Reels and Watch: `Hide Like on reels`, `Hide Comment on reels` and `Hide Share on reels` take that button off the side of a reel, next to the Save and WhatsApp switches that were already there (Refs #151, Refs #265).

- `Hide dislike on comments` under Comments and writing takes the thumbs-down off comments, the one Facebook puts next to Like on reels and videos. Like and Reply stay. It starts off (Refs #241).

- `Hide posts from Pages` under News feed takes posts written by Pages out of the feed, the Pages you follow included. Friends' and group posts stay, and so does a friend's share of a Page's post. It starts off (Refs #262).

Fixes

- With `See-through bars` on, a blurred strip no longer hangs above the bottom tab bar while it slides away or comes back. The blur used to spread past the bar's edge whenever the bar was partly faded (Refs #250, #124).

- With `Picture-in-picture` off, reels no longer shrink into a floating window when you leave Facebook. Some accounts get Facebook's own version of that window, switched on from Facebook's side or from its Media settings, and it used to slip past the switch (Refs #252, #256).

- With `Open feed videos on their own` on, a regular video post in your feed (one that isn't a reel) starts as fast as it does with the switch off. That now includes video posts you open from inside a group. Their full screen viewer used to sit on a blank loading screen first, for up to a second on the home feed and two seconds or more in a group. Reels you open from the feed still play alone with nothing after them (Refs #237).

- With `Tap to play` on, a video you open from a comment plays in Facebook's full screen player again. It used to sit paused there until you left Facebook and came back (Refs #242).

Other changes

- You need Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer now. The patches are built on Morphe patcher 2.0.1, which uses less memory while patching, and older Managers refuse a bundle built on it, so update Manager first. Desktop patching needs morphe-desktop 1.19.1 or newer.

- Hush titles are drawn in Facebook's blues now, shifting slowly with a light sheen moving across. That covers the settings bar and search, Hush dialogs, the screen shown when settings can't open, and the lock cover. Every color stays readable on its background in every theme, and the titles keep moving even with Android's animations off.

- Long sections are easier to scan. News feed, Reels and Watch, Video and audio, Appearance and Pause, backup and diagnostics group their rows under small headings like `Content filters`, `Video quality` and `Troubleshooting`, still right on the main page. Where the tab bar sits, what it does while you scroll, which tabs hide and their dots all moved to a new Tabs and navigation section. `Tab bar position` and `Tab bar while scrolling` are each one pick from three now, with Facebook's own behavior first, so the two old switches can't fight each other.

- A few names got clearer. Playback is Video and audio, Links is Links and sharing, Chats is Chats and Messenger, and Set when you patched is Built-in changes. Writing joined Comments, and the quality row reads `Default quality`. Search still finds everything by its old name. `Save crashes to Downloads` moved from Privacy to Troubleshooting, right above Pause, and Support keeps help and restart apart from supporting the project.

- `Hide posts with words you choose` now reads a shared link's headline and the line under it too, so a news post whose only mention of a word is in its link preview hides. That includes the newer cards Facebook draws from its own layout, where the headline isn't a plain field. A keep word on the preview still keeps the post (Refs #255).

- The `Only from a reel's More menu` description says which reels get the Picture-in-picture row. Upright reels do, wide ones never did, and the old wording made a missing row look like a bug (Refs #252).

- Patching with `Material You theme` on is faster. Its scans now skip the parts of Facebook they can't change, and the patched app comes out the same as before (Refs #236).

- The README now explains how to go back to an earlier release that lists your Facebook version. You add its bundle as a local source in Manager, patch with the same key and install over your copy. Sign-in and settings stay, and the README lists what `Export settings` leaves out. The steps follow Manager 2.2's own screens and cover what to do when Manager reports a Package conflict instead of installing.

- `Accent color` works with the Material You theme now. It used to sit greyed out whenever Material You was patched in. Now the color you pick replaces your wallpaper's accent and the wallpaper's greys stay, while the first choice, `Wallpaper accent`, keeps the phone's own. It's picked in Hushfacebook's settings under Appearance with no repatch, and Facebook picks it up after a restart (Refs #272).

Behind the scenes

- A device walk no longer fails a page because something an earlier step left open is sitting on top of it. On the S22 the long press on a reel left a comment sheet over the next page, and the Notifications step failed on two walks in a row. When a page can't be confirmed, the walk now presses Back once and opens the link again. Checked in the audit's tests.

- The device walk reads the phone's screen text as UTF-8. Started from Git Bash, it read it in the console's old code page, so the curly apostrophe in a notification's settings button never matched and the Notifications step failed on a page that was right there. Checked in the audit's tests.

- Device audits read their settings snapshots in Windows PowerShell too, so the push check no longer fails every restore case where git can't find pwsh.

- The source audit reads the Morphe Patch Tracker in Windows PowerShell too. The tracker now lists two bundles whose names differ only by capital letters, and when git couldn't find pwsh the push check stopped on it.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.2.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `584.0.0.51.56`. On most phones that's build `475817393`, the arm64-v8a one. Phones with a 32-bit processor take build `475817404`, the armeabi-v7a one.
3. Install over your current patched Facebook with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Facebook APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook#install).

Look over a diagnostic report before you share it. The filter can still miss private text it doesn't recognize.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 3928 tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 105 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 584.0.0.51.56, both the 64-bit and the 32-bit build, and a second build of the same commit matched this bundle entry for entry (820 entries). I patched Facebook with this exact bundle and walked the whole app with every switch on, on an emulator signed in to a full account. 79 of 106 hook families ran there, `Hide the Create button`, `Tap to play` and `Don't save search history` among them, all 23 settings pages opened in dark and in light, and Facebook didn't crash once. Android's verifier raised nothing on the patched build, the same as on Meta's own. The walk doesn't reach downloads, chats or the story viewer, so those are covered by the patch tests alone this time, and the 32-bit build was checked by its patch tests rather than on a device.

hushmessenger.body:
HushMessenger 0.27.0 moves to Messenger 584.1.0.61.98 and works with every arm64 and armv7 build APKMirror has for it. Log out is back on the App tab, and new switches give you square profile pictures and keep Your story out of the share list.There's also an optional white on black launcher icon. The settings got a cleaner layout with folding sections, and a clone install no longer crashes when the regular Messenger is on the same phone.

You'll need Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer.

### New in this release

- **Log out** is back. It's a row on the App page of the HushMessenger settings, and tapping it signs you out of the account on this phone the same way Messenger's own Log out does. You end up on Messenger's login screen, ready for the same account or a different one. There's no extra "are you sure" step. If a Messenger build ever moves its Log out, the row says so and points you to the one in Messenger's menu. Refs #88.
- **Square profile pictures** is a new switch under Theme, and it starts off. After a restart, profile pictures in the chat list, the stories row, chat headers and suggestions turn into squares, or rounded squares if you also turn on **Round the corners**. People who are online, the ones with the green dot, keep the same size as everyone else in the stories row. Notification pictures stay round. Refs #89.
- **Custom launcher icon** is a new patch that starts unselected. It turns Messenger's home screen icon white on black, or black on white if you pick that style, using Messenger's own logo. Themed icons on Android 13 and up still work. Patch again without it to get the normal icon back. Refs #107.
- HushMessenger's settings speak Traditional Chinese when your phone is set to it, in Taiwan, Hong Kong or Macau. Simplified Chinese still shows English for now. Thanks to @JhouHank for the translation. Refs #98.
- **Hide Your story when sharing** is a new switch under Photos and videos, and it starts off. Share a photo, video or link into Messenger from another app and the Send to list won't offer Your story anymore, so a stray tap on Add can't post it. Your chats and groups stay right where they were, and the story itself works as usual. Refs #102.

### Fixes and changes

- HushMessenger now targets Messenger 584.1.0.61.98 and takes all 21 builds APKMirror lists for it, arm64 and armv7 alike, including the three arm64 bundles `346817008`, `346817025` and `346817026`. 584.0.0.49.98 is no longer supported, so update Messenger before you patch. Each build was checked patch by patch, and Morphe Desktop applied and rebuilt every one of them. Refs #106.
- Patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.0.1, which uses less memory while patching. You'll need Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer, or Morphe Desktop 1.19.1.
- The HushMessenger settings got a tighter layout, modeled on HushFacebook's. Every section folds up under its own header and starts closed, so the whole list fits on a couple of screens. Open the ones you use and they stay open next time. Searching still finds any control, whether its section is open or not. The banner with "Make Messenger yours" and the Inbox, Chats and More chips are gone. The colors now follow Messenger's own blue in both the light and dark theme, and Restart Messenger sits at the top of the App tab.
- Every HushMessenger title (the settings name, the sheet titles and the restart screen) now shows Messenger's blue to purple to pink to orange colors. They drift slowly with a light sheen now and then, and they keep moving even with Android's animations turned off.
- TalkBack reads each settings section's open or closed state once now. It used to say it twice, like "collapsed, Collapsed, Inbox".
- With large text, the little arrow on each settings section shows whole again. At 200% it was cut down to a sliver.
- **Source and licenses** under About opens the README's Credits section again. It pointed at a heading the README no longer has, so it landed at the top of the page.
- With **Open your gallery app** on and no default gallery set, the list Android shows you now holds only your gallery apps. It could slip in other pickers, like Contacts. Whichever gallery you tap still opens with your photos and videos together. Refs #94.
- If Messenger crashed in the last three days, **Report a problem** now adds a line saying where in the code it happened. It's only the names of the failing code, never the error text, so no file names or chat content go in. Refs #103.
- Checking what you picked from your gallery no longer holds up Messenger's screen. If you cancel, or the pick times out or loses its permission, you're back in the chat with nothing attached. Report a problem now notes how the last gallery pick ended, without any file names. Refs #94.
- The patch log now shows when each search through Messenger's code starts and finishes. The Wi-Fi search is faster and lighter on memory too, since it reads Messenger's code directly instead of building text for every reference it passes. Refs #93, #99, #100.
- In **Auto reply**, a picture always lands on the card you picked it for, and it's always the one you picked last. Before, a slow copy of an earlier pick could finish late and replace the newer picture, or put one back after you tapped Clear. Save waits while a picture is still copying.
- Picking a picture for an auto reply is safer with huge or slow files. HushMessenger reads the file once into its own copy, turns away files over 32 MB or 64 megapixels, and gives up after 30 seconds, then tells you which of those happened. Picking again or tapping Clear stops the earlier copy right away, and the picture you had before stays put.
- Some APKMirror downloads of Messenger only carry icons for one small screen size, so on a sharper phone the launcher icon and the icons in Messenger's settings look blurry and jagged. HushMessenger's settings now say so under About when your download is one of those, and the README lists which builds have icons for every screen. Patching a `nodpi` build fixes it. Refs #91.
- **Hide Meta AI** now reaches the search screen too. Tap the search bar and the box at the top used to say "Ask Meta AI or search" even with the switch on. Now it shows the plain search hint, like the bar on the Chats list. Search still finds people and chats the same way.
- **Clone install under another package name** no longer crashes a few seconds after you open the copy when the regular Messenger is on the phone too. The copy was saving its muted chats into the other Messenger's storage, which Android blocks, so now it keeps them in its own.
- With **Slide chats in and out** on, a chat whose first frames come late no longer jumps partway in. That happened most on the first chat you open after starting Messenger. The chat now waits off screen until Messenger draws on time (a quarter second at most), then slides in from the edge. Going back works the same way.

### Behind the scenes

- The install check now names the kind of refusal it finds and what to do about it. A Messenger signed with another key says which Android user it's installed for, so a copy hiding in Secure Folder or a work profile is easy to find. A permission held by another app (`INSTALL_FAILED_DUPLICATE_PERMISSION`) is no longer mixed up with a Messenger signer problem.
- The README's settings screenshots are new, and they now show the App tab too. They're rendered from the settings code, with a small record of which switches they show and each image's checksum. A release stops when a switch was added, renamed or retired since then, or when an image no longer matches. Any link from the app into the README has to reach a heading that exists.
- When another app takes the phone's screen in the middle of a walk, the failed step now says which app it was, instead of only saying it left no screen dump.
- The whole-app walk now has to show every screen it opened. Counting them is no longer enough. Each required step (a chat, both settings tabs, the message log and auto reply sheets when those patches are in, and each native screen) saves a screenshot and a UI dump next to the receipt, with their checksums. Publish reads those files again and refuses the walk when a step is missing or listed twice, a file is missing or changed, a screen shows the Restore or login prompt, two steps landed on the same screen, or a step ended up somewhere it shouldn't. An older receipt that only counted screens doesn't count anymore.
- Every Messenger screen in the walk now has to land on its own page. Any Messenger screen no longer passes. Each step checks the page it lands on and a label only that page has, so a link that drops back to the inbox fails. Messenger 584.1 ignores most of its old links when another app sends them (the inbox, Active now, stories, new message, stickers and Marketplace). The walk now opens the inbox from Messenger's own launcher and adds the story and contact settings pages, which still open by link.
- On Android 12 and older the walk can now pass the message log. Before Android 13 the log blocks screenshots to keep chat text out of Recents, so that one step keeps a record showing its window is locked instead. Every other step still needs its screenshot.

### Reports this release changed something for

#88 Log out, #89 square profile pictures, #94 gallery app list, #98 Traditional Chinese, #102 Your story in the share list, #103 crash details in Report a problem, #106 Messenger 584.1, #107 launcher icon, and #91, #93, #99 and #100.

Full history is in the [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

### How to update

1. Update Messenger to 584.1.0.61.98 first. 584.0 won't patch with this release. Any build on [APKMirror's 584.1.0.61.98 page](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/facebook-2/messenger/facebook-messenger-584-1-0-61-98-release/) works, and a `nodpi` one keeps the icons sharp.
2. In Morphe Manager, open **Sources** and refresh HushMessenger. The card should say **66 patches**.
3. Patch Messenger again and install it over your current one. Your settings carry over.

Patching on a computer? `patches-0.27.0.mpp` below is the same bundle for Morphe Desktop 1.19.1 or newer. It's a patch bundle, not a Messenger APK. `SHA256SUMS.txt` and its signature let you check the download, and the README says how.

### What was checked

- The full test suite, plus a patch run against every Messenger 584.1 build on file.
- Morphe Desktop patched and rebuilt one APK from each of the four build families.
- An APK patched from this exact bundle was installed on a Galaxy S22 over a signed-in Messenger. The chat, inbox, both HushMessenger settings tabs, the message log, auto reply and Messenger's own settings, story and contact pages all opened, with no crashes.

hushfeed.title: v0.79.0
hushfeed.body:
Hushfeed v0.79.0 has 141 patches. 140 of them are for global TikTok 47.5.3 (`com.zhiliaoapp.musically`), and 95 work on PineDrama 47.5.3, one of those made just for it. It needs Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer, since it's built on patcher 2.0.0.

TikTok stays on 47.5.3, so the TikTok APK you already have is fine to patch again. PineDrama moves to 47.5.3, so grab that one from APKMirror before you patch it. PineDrama got a lot of attention in this one. Six more patches run on it, and photo comments and imported fonts work there now. On TikTok there's a spam comment filter and a way to record a LIVE straight off the screen, and `Hide videos you have already seen` keeps watched videos out of For You again.

Here's every report this release changed something for, and what changed.

For bug reports

* Repeats in For You (#172). `Hide videos you have already seen` checks each new For You page once TikTok hands it over, so videos you watched stop coming back.
* The comment bar on photo posts (#171). With `AMOLED dark theme`, the `Add comment...` bar under a photo post is black instead of letting the photo show through.
* Fonts on PineDrama (#243). `Use an imported font` now draws PineDrama's text in your font, and bold text stays bold.
* Missing saved stickers (#214). PineDrama's sticker panel loads every sticker you saved. It used to stop at 100.
* Low download quality (#240). When the quality list stops below 720p, it also offers the video's own H.264 or HEVC file if that one is taller, and the diagnostic report shows why each quality was or wasn't offered.
* Commenter countries (#201). `Show where commenters are from` remembers people's countries from their earlier comments and videos, so it finds one more often.
* Running out of memory while patching (#220). The README says to give morphe-desktop 2 GB with `java -Xmx2g`.
* Automatic Clear display (#84). A search result you open again clears again, even if you brought its buttons back by hand last time.

For feature requests

* PineDrama (#156). It moves to 47.5.3, six more patches run on it, and a new `Allow photo comments` patch lets the comment box ask TikTok's server about photo comments like TikTok does. Hushfeed's settings also say to restart PineDrama now, not TikTok.
* A spam shield for comments (#187). `Hide spam comments` hides the bots that point you to their bio or hand out a contact, and leaves the creator's own comments alone.
* Effects that refuse older phones (#176). `Report a newer phone to effects` tells the effects server you have a Galaxy S24 Ultra.
* Saving LIVEs (#37). `LIVE recording source` can record the screen as you watch, and Share > Video quality now shows in gaming and football rooms too.
* LIVE recording presets (#203). `LIVE recording quality` offers Original, 1080p, 720p, 540p and 360p and takes a room's 60 fps stream when it has one. You can change it from a LIVE room's Share sheet too.
* The liquid glass bar (#231). `Blur the video behind the bar` frosts the pill with the video under it, and the lens slides between tabs every time now.
* Dark LIVE rooms (#159). The light bits left in rooms turn dark, from the profile card's tiles to the menu's navigation bar, and a room stays dark when your phone switches themes.
* The Auto scroll switch on foldables (#234). `Hide TikTok's Auto scroll button` hides the switch beside the avatar too, with or without Auto-advance.
* OmerKurdi79's batch (#232). Clear display lets go with your swipe, and the See-through bottom bar no longer drops the caption over the tabs after each swipe.
* An instant pause (#239). With double tap set to do nothing, a tap pauses or plays the moment your finger lifts.
* Latest on Following (#226). `Latest first` keeps everything below your video in date order as posts load, and the tab starts on the newest post.
* Better sorting (#180). Profile grids get Least viewed first and Least liked first. While an order is on, the grid loads up to 300 videos by itself, and swiping through them keeps that order.
* Stories from LIVE creators (#233). `Open the Story when a creator is LIVE` opens their Story from their profile picture or your chat with them, and the next tap joins the LIVE.
* LIVE quality in dark mode (#57). The newer Video quality picker in a LIVE room's menu is readable on dark mode.
* Add to Story (#88). `Allow Add to Story anyway` brings the button back when a creator turned off content reuse.
* Time zones (#184, #198). With `Match locale and timezone` on, chat dates follow the preset's zone.
* Thoughts (#186). `Turn on Thoughts` shows Thoughts for accounts TikTok left out.
* Original image formats (#229). Stickers that don't move are saved as TikTok sent them too.
* Camera brightness (#200). `Keep the screen's brightness in the camera` also covers the front flash and the fill light.
* Region locked features (#98). Feature Gate Lab's `Scrolling comments on videos` preset says up front that only some videos get scrolling comments.

## What's changed

* On PineDrama, Hushfeed's settings now tell you to restart PineDrama instead of TikTok. That covers the note under each switch, the restart button that shows up once you flip one, the saved message and the Feature Gate Lab, in English and all nine translations. Other mentions of TikTok, like its servers or the TikTok Sans font, stay as they are (#156).
* New `Hide spam comments` switch in Hushfeed settings > Comments, off by default (#187). It hides bot comments that send you to their profile or a "link in bio", spell out a website, hand out a Telegram or WhatsApp contact, or offer free followers. It knows the common phrasings in English and the languages Hushfeed's settings come in, plus French. Your own comments stay, and so do the creator's and any they pinned or liked, so a "part 2 in my bio" from the creator still shows.
* `Hide videos you have already seen` takes watched videos out of For You again (#172). TikTok reads each new page once before handing it to the feed. The switch sits that first read out, as it does on lists you open yourself, but everything the read kept was then remembered as allowed and never checked again. Now the page gets checked against what you've watched once TikTok hands it over, and your watch record starts loading during that first read so it's ready in time.
* With AMOLED dark theme, the `Add comment...` bar under a photo post you open from search, a profile or a link is black now (#171). TikTok leaves that bar see-through, and a photo runs on underneath it, so the photo showed through where a video post shows black.
* `Use an imported font` now works on PineDrama (#243). PineDrama doesn't carry TikTok's own fonts, so its text fell back to your phone's font and the imported one never got used. It now draws in your font at the weight the app asked for, so bold text stays bold.
* Feature Gate Lab's `Scrolling comments on videos` preset tells you before you apply it that comments only scroll on videos TikTok has turned them on for. Each video carries its own flag from TikTok's server, so most videos look the same with the preset on (#98).
* New `Allow photo comments` patch for PineDrama, with its switch off by default (#156). PineDrama hides the gallery tab in the comment box for everyone, even though TikTok's server allows photo comments. Turn the switch on in Hushfeed settings > Comments and restart, and the comment box asks the server like TikTok does.
* PineDrama moves to 47.5.3 and 47.4.3 is dropped, so grab the new PineDrama from APKMirror before you patch it again. Six more patches run on it now: `Advanced downloads`, `Automatic video advance`, `Hide inbox items`, `Hide profile shortcuts`, `Open the comments at full height` and `Show the progress bar`. PineDrama 47.5.3 has no stories, HD upload choice or foldable comment panel, so `Story controls`, `Always upload in HD` and `Foldable split comment view` are TikTok only now. That makes 95 patches Morphe Manager offers for PineDrama. The rest lean on TikTok's LIVE rooms, feed buttons or resources that PineDrama doesn't have (#156).
* New `Report a newer phone to effects` switch, off by default (#176). Effects ask TikTok's server whether your phone can run them, and on some older phones the answer is "This effect doesn't work on this device". With the switch on, the effects server is told you have a Galaxy S24 Ultra. Sign-in and everything else still see your real phone. An effect your phone really can't run may still fail or look wrong.
* New `Load all saved stickers` patch, with no switch. PineDrama's sticker panel loaded only the first 100 stickers you saved and never asked for more, so the rest were missing from Saved. It now asks for all of them in one go. TikTok gets the same first request, and it still loads more by itself past that (#214).
* New `LIVE recording source` choice under `Record LIVEs you watch`. `Stream only` saves the room's own video like before. `Screen` records what your phone shows while you watch. Android asks to allow screen recording each time, and Stop saves it. The app's sound comes along when TikTok has the microphone permission, otherwise the recording is video only (#37).

hushgram.title: v0.0.17
hushgram.body:
HushGram moves to Instagram 453.0.0.55.79, and Morphe Manager now knows all four of its builds, so 32-bit phones get pointed at the right one. Stories can play with a seek bar, a thicker progress bar and rounded corners, and reels you open from Home can start with sound. Home can keep your place when you come back, carousels can peek at the next page, and a chat's shared reels can be swiped through in a row. Settings got a new look in Instagram's blues, with sections that open in place, and there's a long list of fixes for downloads, the lock and the glass tab bar.

New in this release

- `Keep your place in Home`: New switch under Feed. Coming back to Instagram leaves Home on the post you were on, however long you were away. Instagram no longer reloads it or resets the app to the top. Pull down still refreshes. Starts off. Asked for in #354.

- `Glass tab bar`: `Hide the tab bar as you scroll` works with the glass off too. Scroll down and Instagram's own bar slides away while the page fills its space. Scroll up and it's back. Reels keep their bar. Asked for in #343.

- `Rounded post corners`: `Rounded corners on Reels` under Feed rounds a reel's video in the Reels tab and full screen, at the same Corner size. The seek bar, captions and buttons stay whole. Starts off. Asked for in #362.

- `Rounded post corners`: `Rounded corners on stories` under Feed rounds a story's photo or video, whether it opens from the tray, a profile or a highlight, at the same Corner size. The progress bar, names and stickers stay whole. Starts off. Asked for in #363 and #368.

- `Rounded post corners`: `Peek at the next carousel page` under Feed sits each carousel page in from the edges, with the start of the next page showing at the right. Starts off. Asked for in #361.

- `Thicker story progress bar`: new patch. `Thicker story progress bar` under Stories draws the bar along the top of a story twice or three times as thick. Its segments and timing don't change. Starts off. Asked for in #360.

- `Start reels with sound`: new patch. `Start reels with sound` under Playback plays a reel you tap open from a post on Home with sound, and Home is muted again when you go back. Starts off. Asked for in #342.

- `Pick the app icon`: `App icon` adds Instagram in black on white, a white icon with Instagram's glyph in black. Themed icons still show Instagram's glyph. Asked for in #353.

- `Tab bar layout`: new patch. `Tab bar layout` under Tab bar keeps the newer bar, where you swipe between every tab, or the classic one, even when Instagram switches your account. Starts on Instagram's choice. Asked for in #356.

- `Lock your messages`: `Double-tap Messages for hidden chats` under Messages opens your hidden chats from two quick taps on the Messages button, after the lock when one's on. One tap still opens Messages. Starts off. Asked for in #358.

- `HushGram settings`: A build without Pure black dark mode now says under Layout how to get it: pick it in Morphe Manager next time you patch. Searching settings for "amoled" or "oled" finds it too. Asked for in #359.

- `Download any video`: `Choose a folder` under Downloads sends every photo and video to a folder you pick, a hidden one too, and it works on Android 9 without the storage permission. `Use Movies and Pictures` puts saves back. Asked for in #333.

- `Seek bar on stories`: new patch. `Seek bar on stories` under Stories puts a bar near the bottom of a video story. Drag it to jump anywhere in the video and the story plays on from there. Starts off. Asked for in #355.

- `Swipe through a chat's reels`: new patch. With `Swipe through a chat's reels` on under Messages, swiping up on a reel opened from a chat goes through the chat's other shared reels before any suggested ones. Starts off. Asked for in #350.

- `Hide suggested stories`: `Filter the Stories tray by verified accounts` under Stories keeps only verified accounts in the row at the top of Home, or only the ones that aren't. Your own story stays. Starts off. Asked for in #340.

Fixes

- `Show if a profile follows you`: On your Following list, Doesn't follow you now comes before the name. A long name used to push it off the end of the line. Reported in #351.

- `Hide the emoji row` and `Hide Follow on posts` now work the moment you switch them on. Before, nothing changed until you left Instagram and came back.

- `Hide suggested stories` adds `Keep the Stories tray in the feed` under Stories. On some accounts the row floated over Home mid-feed and stayed put while posts scrolled under it. Now it stays in the feed. Starts off. Reported in #357.

- Morphe Manager now knows the armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64 builds of Instagram too, so an older 32-bit phone is pointed at the build it can install instead of the arm64 one. Reported in #346.

- `Glass tab bar` no longer leaves a dark band under a reel opened from the feed, where Instagram hides the tab bar. Reels opened from the Reels tab still stop above the bar. Reported in #347.

- `Start stories with sound` turns Instagram's sound back off when you leave a story, so Feed and Reels stay muted. Coming back to the story turns it on again, and a story you muted yourself stays muted. Reported in #342.

- `Download any story` also adds Download to the menu of your own highlights, which Instagram builds differently from other story menus. Reported in #339.

- `Hide Follow on feed posts` also filters Subscribe before the feed header builds it. The author's name, time and menu keep their native paths.

- `Tap to play` keeps a Reels auto-scroll allowance for the next Reel. Feed and unidentified players can't spend it, and a real tap on Feed still works.

- `Group Instagram's notifications` keeps summaries while their notifications remain. Turning grouping off or removing one notification no longer dismisses the others. Pending posts stay protected while Android catches up. One notification uses the singular count label.

- Turning off profile posts as a list, or pausing HushGram, cancels an automatic opening that was still waiting for the grid.

- Canceling a download can finish while DNS, proxy discovery or response setup is still waiting. Late responses can't write a file, and repeated cancellations keep a bounded number of workers.

- The downloader closes opened response streams on success and failure. Cache bytes stay only after a successful close.

- Closing `Save profile picture` stops its fetch even when the general background workers are busy.

- `Download any video` adds source metadata to JPEG photos saved through Save all and Choose pages, as it does for a single photo. Videos and other image formats stay unchanged.

- Download history repairs a partially written record before its next write. Later saves remain listed after a restart.

- A failed PIN save keeps the setup form open and reports the failure. The PIN and its retry counters are saved together.

- PIN retry limits still apply in the current process when their counters can't be saved.

- `HushGram settings` saves a timed lock and its wait together. Lock, unlock and wait actions no longer report success after a failed write.

- `HushGram settings` checks the current lock before an editor or delayed action saves. Imports and Undo check again at their write boundary, and a held Undo remains available until its original deadline.

- Font imports finish reading and closing their provider before replacing a live font. Failed or stale imports leave the current files alone, and reopening settings can't start a competing copy.

- Replacing an imported app font keeps Restart now available even when the font choice hasn't changed.

- Settings backups restore large selections of hidden Instagram settings rows. Selecting all 161 supported rows no longer causes that choice to be skipped.

- `Hide suggested posts` keeps native paging when a filtered page retains a real post, even before its list is displayed. Header-only pages can still finish.

- `Glass tab bar` blur recovers after a temporary capture failure on a still screen. Automatic retries stay bounded, and pending work stops when the bar leaves or HushGram pauses.

- `Story text fonts` puts local fonts before Instagram's paid section, so selecting one doesn't open a Plus offer. Instagram's paid fonts keep their subscription checks. Reported in #275 and #325.

- `View stories anonymously` keeps your own story, Create and special tray entries in their original positions during watched-story sorting. Ordinary story rings keep their order within the unseen and watched groups.

- `HushGram settings` requires Android 9 on every ABI, including the two 32-bit APKs Instagram ships for Android 8. Manifest checks verify that floor and preserve any higher vendor minimum.

- `Show if a profile follows you` waits for unique followers to match the account's count before recording recent unfollowers. Short lists and older queued saves can't replace a newer snapshot, and failed saves can be retried.

- `HushGram settings` lets go of a closed screen or dialog. The moving title used to keep every one you'd opened in memory until Instagram restarted.

- `Convert to keep the full size` asks the phone's encoder for limited range BT.709 color. Left to choose, some encoders write a file other apps show with shifted colors.

Other changes

- HushGram now patches Instagram 453.0.0.55.79 instead of 452.1.0.53.64. Get APKMirror's (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 9.0+) variant, build 385914283. The armeabi-v7a build (385914282) is declared too, and so are the x86 and x86_64 builds (385914284 and 385914285). Thanks to toidicakhia for #366.

- HushGram's settings use Instagram's own blues instead of pink. Switches and buttons take its indigo button color, while icons and headings use the lighter blue Instagram gives links on a dark screen.

- Every HushGram title wears Instagram's gradient now, including the settings bar, its dialogs and the lock screen. The colors drift slowly and a sheen sweeps across every few seconds, even with Android's animations turned off.

- Settings categories expand their controls directly underneath. Several sections can stay open, and tapping a heading collapses it. Search finds controls across every section and restores your open sections when cleared.

- Settings put switches with the screen they change. The Notifications page's suggestion switches moved to Notifications, the Reels tab's to Tab bar, and anonymous DM photos to Messages. Searching their old section still finds them.

- The Updates section in settings is now called Version warnings, since all it holds is the switch for Instagram's "this version is too old" screen. Searching for Updates still finds it.

- Settings open on Ads and privacy now. Settings entry moved down next to backup and the other upkeep sections, after the everyday controls.

- Pause and diagnostics folds like the other sections now, so Debug logging and the report rows don't fill the overview. It opens by itself while HushGram is paused, the settings are locked or a save was interrupted.

- Settings opens with Search, the list view option and a compact category list with shorter descriptions. Quick setups and the active-status banner are gone. Larger text still wraps.

- Download file names support `{shortcode}`, using the parent post's code for carousel pages. Unknown codes are left out. Photo names use the template when it includes that token.

- `Date in backup file names` adds the local date and time to settings exports. It starts off, keeping the existing backup name until enabled.

- Added Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), contributed by JhouHank in #313. Traditional Chinese script preferences and Hong Kong or Macao locales use the new table.

- Hide the emoji row, Hide Follow on posts, Rounded corners on Reels and Thicker story progress bar now share one check before each frame. With several on, Instagram does that work once per frame instead of once for each.

Behind the scenes

- Cached patch lookups now refresh when classes are added, replaced or removed. Unchanged classes keep their cached reads.

- Release walkthroughs require matching bundle, candidate and installed APK evidence, with visible content for each required destination. Incomplete receipts, changed installs and covered pages can't authorize publication.

- Walk navigation checks the chosen tap point, including covers over a partly visible control. Settings labels keep their own location when a row handles the tap.

- The walk accepts a loaded Explore grid under Instagram's empty Compose layer. A labeled, clickable, focusable, filled or differently built layer still counts as a cover.

- The release walk expands each settings category in place and checks it folds again, since Back now closes settings. A row only counts under its own heading, and every row is checked against the settings source.

- The source census keeps a relicensed source's old licence pinned and records code it took from elsewhere. InstaEclipse is GPL-3.0 now, and the HushGram downloader it carries counts as ours. Stylus dropped its Instagram patch.

- The build moves to the Morphe patches plugin 2.0.0 and Kotlin 2.4.21, held to one version across the plugin's classpath. Patched apps come out the same, and the bundle carries Kotlin stdlib 2.4.21.

- The patching help explains the small-heap limit and keeps Manager's embedded VM workaround.

- Updated to Morphe patcher 2.0.1 and its matching Smali library. Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer is required. The dependency audit separately reviews Morphe Desktop 1.19.1.

- GitHub release notes now read like Hushfacebook's. A short summary comes first, then plain grouped bullets with no Instagram label, the update steps and what was checked.

- The bundle now carries Gson 2.15.0. The patch catalog comes out byte for byte the same, and new tests hold its key order, nulls and unescaped text, including emoji.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.2.0 or newer, then refresh the HushGram source.
2. Patch Instagram `453.0.0.55.79`. [Supported Instagram builds](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram#supported-instagram-builds) lists the builds that work.
3. Install over your current patched Instagram with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not an Instagram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram#install).

What was checked

6891 runtime tests passed locally. All 2181 patch tests passed too.

All four Instagram 453.0.0.55.79 builds took 122 of the 123 patches, everything but Install next to Instagram, which makes a second app. I patched Instagram with this exact bundle and walked the whole app on an emulator: the feed, Explore, Reels, the inbox, a profile and every section of HushGram's settings, 29 screens in all, and Instagram didn't crash once.

- HushGram now patches Instagram 453.0.0.55.79 instead of 452.1.0.53.64. Get APKMirror's (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 9.0+) variant, build 385914283. The armeabi-v7a build (385914282) is declared too, and so are the x86 and x86_64 builds (385914284 and 385914285). Thanks to toidicakhia for #366.

- HushGram's settings use Instagram's own blues instead of pink. Switches and buttons take its indigo button color, while icons and headings use the lighter blue Instagram gives links on a dark screen.

- Every HushGram title wears Instagram's gradient now, including the settings bar, its dialogs and the lock screen. The colors drift slowly and a sheen sweeps across every few seconds, even with Android's animations turned off.

- Settings categories expand their controls directly underneath. Several sections can stay open, and tapping a heading collapses it. Search finds controls across every section and restores your open sections when cleared.

- Settings put switches with the screen they change. The Notifications page's suggestion switches moved to Notifications, the Reels tab's to Tab bar, and anonymous DM photos to Messages. Searching their old section still finds them.

- The Updates section in settings is now called Version warnings, since all it holds is the switch for Instagram's "this version is too old" screen. Searching for Updates still finds it.

- Settings open on Ads and privacy now. Settings entry moved down next to backup and the other upkeep sections, after the everyday controls.

- Pause and diagnostics folds like the other sections now, so Debug logging and the report rows don't fill the overview. It opens by itself while HushGram is paused, the settings are locked or a save was interrupted.

- Settings opens with Search, the list view option and a compact category list with shorter descriptions. Quick setups and the active-status banner are gone. Larger text still wraps.

- Download file names support `{shortcode}`, using the parent post's code for carousel pages. Unknown codes are left out. Photo names use the template when it includes that token.

- `Date in backup file names` adds the local date and time to settings exports. It starts off, keeping the existing backup name until enabled.

- Added Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), contributed by JhouHank in #313. Traditional Chinese script preferences and Hong Kong or Macao locales use the new table.

- Hide the emoji row, Hide Follow on posts, Rounded corners on Reels and Thicker story progress bar now share one check before each frame. With several on, Instagram does that work once per frame instead of once for each.

Behind the scenes

- Cached patch lookups now refresh when classes are added, replaced or removed. Unchanged classes keep their cached reads.

- Release walkthroughs require matching bundle, candidate and installed APK evidence, with visible content for each required destination. Incomplete receipts, changed installs and covered pages can't authorize publication.

- Walk navigation checks the chosen tap point, including covers over a partly visible control. Settings labels keep their own location when a row handles the tap.

- The walk accepts a loaded Explore grid under Instagram's empty Compose layer. A labeled, clickable, focusable, filled or differently built layer still counts as a cover.

- The release walk expands each settings category in place and checks it folds again, since Back now closes settings. A row only counts under its own heading, and every row is checked against the settings source.

- The source census keeps a relicensed source's old licence pinned and records code it took from elsewhere. InstaEclipse is GPL-3.0 now, and the HushGram downloader it carries counts as ours. Stylus dropped its Instagram patch.

- The build moves to the Morphe patches plugin 2.0.0 and Kotlin 2.4.21, held to one version across the plugin's classpath. Patched apps come out the same, and the bundle carries Kotlin stdlib 2.4.21.

- The patching help explains the small-heap limit and keeps Manager's embedded VM workaround.

- Updated to Morphe patcher 2.0.1 and its matching Smali library. Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer is required. The dependency audit separately reviews Morphe Desktop 1.19.1.

- GitHub release notes now read like Hushfacebook's. A short summary comes first, then plain grouped bullets with no Instagram label, the update steps and what was checked.

- The bundle now carries Gson 2.15.0. The patch catalog comes out byte for byte the same, and new tests hold its key order, nulls and unescaped text, including emoji.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.2.0 or newer, then refresh the HushGram source.
2. Patch Instagram `453.0.0.55.79`. [Supported Instagram builds](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram#supported-instagram-builds) lists the builds that work.
3. Install over your current patched Instagram with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not an Instagram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram#install).

What was checked

6891 runtime tests passed locally. All 2181 patch tests passed too.

All four Instagram 453.0.0.55.79 builds took 122 of the 123 patches, everything but Install next to Instagram, which makes a second app. I patched Instagram with this exact bundle and walked the whole app on an emulator: the feed, Explore, Reels, the inbox, a profile and every section of HushGram's settings, 29 screens in all, and Instagram didn't crash once.

hushthreads.title: v0.0.16
hushthreads.body:
HushThreads v0.0.16 has 20 patches for Threads 452.0.0.50.64 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so you need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer. Update Threads to 452 before you patch.

Hide ads now also goes after the ads Threads fetches for the replies under an opened post. There's a new `Disable swipe to Search` patch too, for accounts where a sideways swipe on the feed slides into Search.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#12](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/12) found ads among the replies when you open a post. Those come with the post rather than through the feed, and Hide ads now empties that list as well.
- [#13](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/13) asked for a way to stop the feed sliding into Search on a sideways swipe. Turn on `No swipe into Search` on the Feed page and restart Threads. The Search button still works.

## Threads

- HushThreads now patches Threads 452.0.0.50.64 only, the newest stable version, and drops 451.0.0.51.80. Update Threads to 452 before you patch. The bundle is built with Morphe's 2.0 patcher, so you'll need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer.
- Hide ads now also takes out the ads that show up among the replies when you open a post. Threads sends those with the post instead of through your feed, which is how they slipped past before. Turn Hide ads off, or pause HushThreads, and they show the way Threads draws them. The Hide ads switch says so in all six languages.
- New `Disable swipe to Search` patch. On accounts where a sideways swipe on your feed slides into Search, the swipe stops and your feed stays put. The Search button still opens Search. Only some accounts have the swipe, and on the others nothing changes. The `No swipe into Search` switch is on the Feed page of HushThreads settings and starts off. Restart Threads after you flip it.
- A download that runs out of its ten minutes now always says it was too slow. Every so often its last wait ended a fraction of a millisecond early, and you were told the network failed instead.

## Tooling

- A release can't go public until the whole app is walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before the tag or GitHub if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Threads crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` does that walk. It patches Threads from the release bundle and installs it, opens the feed, Search, Activity, a profile and a post by their links, then goes in through the Profile tab, the profile's Settings button and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings and opens every HushThreads settings page. A screen only counts when Threads shows that screen's own view, since a link Threads doesn't handle still opens Threads, on the feed. Any Threads crash or ANR since the walk began fails it, and the receipt it writes is the one publish asks for. Its only taps are those three steps and the settings rows, each checked on its own screen, so it can't follow, block or message anyone, or like a post.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.0.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.16 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Get Threads 452.0.0.50.64 (arm64-v8a, version code 512207626) and patch that. v0.0.15 was the last release for Threads 451.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).

## Validation

1004 runtime tests and 287 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 20 patches applied without forcing to Threads 452.0.0.50.64, and the release receipt records the run. The dependency advisory check passed.

hushtelegram.title: v0.0.21
hushtelegram.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.21 has 67 patches for the Google Play build of Telegram 13.1.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72371) and telegram.org's Telegram 13.1.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72299). telegram.org hasn't moved to 13.1.1 yet, so the two builds sit at different versions this time. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.0.1, so update Morphe Manager to 2.2.0 or newer before you patch. Sixty-three patches are selected by default, and every new switch starts off. A lot of this release came out of your reports. You can hide chats you pick, drop the All Chats tab, keep the text of edited messages, translate into any language Google knows and keep Telegram's downloads in internal storage where file managers can reach them. The settings are one short list now, in Telegram's own blue, and they speak Bulgarian.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** The Google Play build is supported at 13.1.1 now (version code 72371), and Play's 13.1.0 isn't. telegram.org's own download is still 13.1.0 (72299), so that one stays where it was.
* **Telegram:** **Also save from chats that don't allow saving** now takes photos and videos too. Telegram hides Save to Gallery in those chats, so before, only files and songs got copied and the pictures stayed stuck in the app. Each photo and video you open or auto-download there goes to Download/Telegram along with the files. Secret chats and self-destructing media still stay in Telegram, and ordinary chats keep using Save to Gallery. (#29)
* **Telegram:** **Hide folder tab counters** has a new switch on the Chat list page, **Hide picked chats**. Tap **Chats to hide** right under it, tick the chats you'd rather not see, and they leave All Chats, your folders and Archived Chats. A new message doesn't bring them back. They still get their messages and notifications, search still finds them, and nothing changes on your other devices or for anyone else in the chat. Each account keeps its own list. A pinned chat you hide stays pinned, even when you pin or move other chats. The folder tab counts and the app badge still count their unread messages. You can also hide chats straight from the list: long-press them, open the three-dot menu and tap **Hide from chat list**. It's off unless you turn it on. (#24)
* **Telegram:** The Chat list page has a **Hide All Chats** switch right under the folder to open at launch. Turn it on and restart, and the All Chats tab is gone, so the chat list opens on the folder you picked there, or on your first folder if you didn't pick one. Locked folders get skipped, and if you delete the folder you're on, the list moves to the next one you can open. An account with no folders of its own keeps All Chats until you make one. Archived Chats moves into the chat list's three-dot menu and the side menu, since its usual spot sat on top of All Chats. Dragging tabs to reorder them is off while the switch is on (you'll get a short note saying so), so turn it off for a moment to change the order. It's off unless you turn it on. (#21)
* **Telegram:** Every HushTelegram title now uses Telegram's blues, from sky blue to periwinkle. The colors drift slowly along the words, with a light shine every few seconds. That covers the settings header, search and pages like Changed switches, the settings dialogs, the screen shown when settings can't load, and HushTelegram's own pop-ups in chats when Telegram is on a dark theme. It keeps moving even with Android's animations turned off.
* **Telegram:** The HushTelegram settings use Telegram's own blue now instead of cyan, so they look like part of the app. Switches, section titles, buttons and the text cursor all match, and everything still reads clearly on the black background.
* **Telegram:** The HushTelegram settings are one short list now. Every section, from Ads down to About, opens right where it is with a tap and folds away with another, so there's no More settings page to dig through anymore. Rows, icons and the header take less room, and the welcome lines at the top are gone. Pause moved to a button at the top of the screen, and the status card only shows up when it has something to tell you, like a pause waiting on a restart. When a switch needs a restart, the restart row appears right under it, and after the restart the sections you had open are still open.
* **Telegram:** **Keep deleted messages** has a new switch, **Keep edit history**. When someone else edits a message, your phone keeps the text it had before, up to five earlier versions for each of the last 500 edited messages. Open the edited message's menu and tap Message details, which shows up for it even with its own switch off. Each earlier text is listed with the time of the edit, oldest first. **Clear edit history** right under the switch forgets all of it, in every account. Your own messages, disappearing messages and messages from chats that don't allow saving are left alone. It's off unless you turn it on, and the kept text never leaves your phone.
* **Telegram:** Translate with an outside service has a **Translate into** row on the Conversations page, right under Translation service. It lists every language Google's web translate knows (about 250, Dari and Cantonese among them), each by its own name, with a search box that finds a language by its own name, its name in your app's language, its English name or its code. Where your phone knows a language by another name, Google's is shown next to it, like Akan (Twi). Pick Persian, or any other language Telegram's own translate list doesn't offer, and Translate here and Translate this chat both write in it. That works with Google and with your own AI service. Pick Traditional Chinese and messages in Simplified get written out in Traditional too, and the other way around. Telegram's language stays the default, pausing HushTelegram goes back to it, and a settings backup carries the choice. Left on Telegram's language, it writes in the language Telegram's own translate bar shows for the chat, so a language you picked there (in that chat, or last time anywhere) is used. (#35)
* **Telegram:** The keyboard doesn't cover Save and Cancel anymore in the Translation service, chat list title emoji and message filter boxes. The box now shrinks to fit above the keyboard, which matters most with a large font size or on a small screen.
* **Telegram:** With Telegram set to Hebrew, Translate with an outside service leaves Hebrew messages alone instead of writing them out again in Hebrew. Google names Hebrew and Javanese by their older codes, and those now count as the same language.
* **Telegram:** Save downloaded files has a **Gallery folder** row on the Playback page. It picks where Save to Gallery puts the photos and videos you save. Telegram's own Pictures/Telegram and Movies/Telegram stay the default. You can put both in DCIM/Telegram instead, or keep them apart in DCIM/Telegram/Photos and DCIM/Telegram/Videos.
